articles.title: This red state race could spell big trouble for MAGA's post-Trump future: column
articles.description: An instantly infamous Republican attack ad in Ohio may be exposing deep fault lines over what comes after Donald Trump, according to an analysis. In a new column, New York Times columnist Michelle Goldberg wrote that Vivek Ramaswamy, the GOP nominee for Ohio governor, released “what may be the most disgusting ad in American political history.” In doing so, Goldberg argued, he opened “a kind of proxy debate on the right about whether a post-Trump conservatism should try to reclaim some base-line morality or continue along its current smashmouth course.” The ad features the elderly mother of Democratic nominee Amy Acton calling her daughter a liar. Acton was 12 when her stepfather was indicted on charges of raping her. He fled before trial, and her mother stood by him, lost custody of her children and has not seen Acton since 1978. The spot first circulated online without attribution, but as outrage mounted, Ramaswamy’s campaign admitted it was behind the ad, then, “in Trumpian style, doubled down,” vowing to spend millions to air it. “By tacitly siding with a man indicted on charges of child rape," Goldberg wrote, "Ramaswamy has shown us all who he is." Some of the sharpest criticism has come from the right. National Review, which published its “Against Trump” issue in 2016 before becoming one of the president’s “apologists and bootlickers,” Goldberg wrote, has now run several columns lambasting Ramaswamy. Conservative commentator Erick Erickson, who endorsed Trump in 2019 despite misgivings, lamented, “We keep being told we must surrender our decency to win and then we lament how indecent the country is becoming," but Goldberg jabbed that he wrote this “as if he had not been one of the ones counseling such surrender.” Trump and Vice President JD Vance, meanwhile, rallied behind the ad. Vance praised Ramaswamy’s “audacity” and scoffed at Republicans “whining” about it. Trump wrote that he wished “the mothers of my opponents would be so brave as to come forward and explain that their son or daughter is a liar, and much worse.” “Both men seem to understand that Republicans who criticize Ramaswamy are also implicitly criticizing them,” Goldberg wrote. That’s especially true for Vance, Ramaswamy’s friend from Yale Law School, who shares his venture capital and tech-right résumé. Goldberg branded both men “charmless, awkwardly imitating the president’s cruel provocations without his dark charisma or comic timing.” With Trump so unpopular that Republicans risk losing Texas and Kansas, and “the whole gaudy edifice of MAGA” crumbling, the stakes go well beyond Ohio. “If Ramaswamy loses a state as red as Ohio despite Trump’s imprimatur, Vance might start to look like a bad bet in 2028,” Goldberg warned.

articles.description: With elections looming in 2027, Roberto Vannacci’s new far-right movement could fatally outflank the prime minister Giorgia Meloni’s government became the longest serving in Italy’s republican history last month. articles.title: Horror as another suspect polling firm vanishes amid scrutiny: 'Major scandal'
articles.description: The election forecasting community was rattled this week by reporting that Wedgewood Polls, a recent upstart firm, had been fabricating most or all of its data. Now another polling firm is in experts' crosshairs — but they seem to have deleted their entire internet presence before anything could be proven. FiftyPlusOne, a polling analysis site, announced in a blog post on Thursday it is ending its use of SoCal Strategies’ surveys after the pollster’s web presence disappeared a few days after FiftyPlusOne asked to check its data. FiftyPlusOne interviewed a person calling himself Wilson Rochford, the firm’s head pollster, on October 20. He promised to send raw data by Friday to substantiate disputed surveys, and said Jack Sims, who had been tied to Wedgewood, “didn’t actually have a big role” in polling. FiftyPlusOne says it hasn’t heard back since, and that the Washington Post reported the firm’s website and X account were gone. The site says it can’t confirm basic facts about the business or its people. A Florida company Sims set up was dissolved in May, with no replacement found. VoteHub’s Zachary Donnini said the head pollster at Wedgewood told him he attended Boston University and had worked with SoCal Strategies, details that fit Rochford. FiftyPlusOne is removing two SoCal Strategies polls in particular, which it says are missing crosstab data and don't look like any of the rest of the firm's output. The new report triggered shockwaves among social media observers. "This polling situation is a hair's breadth away from becoming a major, major scandal," wrote Fox News Digital columnist David Marcus. "Seems pretty clear at this point that the polling industry needs to be regulated," wrote political columnist Alex Zeldin. "Seems like @50plus1news is becoming the Isaac Chotiner of polling investigations," wrote Blueprint Polls lead pollster Evan Roth Smith.

articles.title: Judge orders Trump deposition in defamation suit against the BBC by Dec. 11
articles.description: A federal judge has ordered President Donald Trump to sit for a deposition in his defamation lawsuit against the BBC by Dec. 11. The order Thursday from U.S. Magistrate Judge Enjoliqué Lett came as the BBC’s lawyers complained that Trump had delayed his appearance. Attorney Charles Tobin said that with two months left in the discovery period, “we still haven’t been able to depose the plaintiff.” Lett said Trump must sit for a deposition by Dec. 11 or face sanctions up to dismissal of his lawsuit unless the discovery period was extended past Dec. 18. Trump is bringing the case over a BBC documentary called “Trump: A Second Chance.”
